target_customer: Hospitals, clinics and health workers in Nigeria and other African and Gulf markets; lenders and governments for financing and data
problem: African healthcare providers relied on paper records and lacked digital operations, billing and affordable financing.
business_model: SaaS for electronic medical records and hospital management, plus lending (HeliumCredit) and payments
product_category: Health tech, EMR and healthcare fintech

founders.name: Adegoke Olubusi
education: Johns Hopkins University, advanced engineering degree (2014)

founders.name: Dimeji Sofowora
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page and by TechCrunch 2020 and 2023.

founders.name: Tito Ovia
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by TechCrunch 2020 and 2023; not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: EMR and hospital management software for low connectivity environments is standard enterprise engineering with local integration challenges.

defensibility.rationale: Hospital systems are sticky once records are digitized, and later lending uses provider data, but early on the software was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source names a well resourced incumbent in Nigerian EMR; Helium Health reached Series B in 2023.

market_need_then: Search and press describe paper based records in African hospitals; the company says it was profitable by 2020 and later reports 500+ providers served.

identity.voice_and_tone: mission driven, claims #1 healthtech in Africa

rebrands.why: A search result says the company was formerly known as One Medical; rebrand date and reason not found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is easy to say, but it collides with the Helium crypto network in search and no brand specific press was found.

pivots.to: Adding healthcare financing (HeliumCredit) and doctor booking via Meddy acquisition
pivots.why: The 2023 Series B coverage says funds go to HeliumCredit; the YC page records the November 2021 Meddy acquisition.

outcome_analysis: Helium Health built an EMR business in Nigeria, raised a $10M Series A in 2020 with Tencent and Global Ventures, acquired Meddy in 2021 and raised a $30M Series B in 2023 to scale healthcare lending. It remains active, receiving a $2.5M Google.org grant, so the path is an expanding infrastructure and fintech play with first funds before 2020 undisclosed.
notes: Outcome search found no shutdown, layoffs or acquisition of Helium Health; it acquired Meddy in Nov 2021 (YC page, location Qatar or UAE inconsistent). A 2017 seed of about $2M with YC and Tencent appears in search text only, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round; total near $42M per aggregators exceeds recorded $40M plus grants. Competitor searches returned no dated 2017 rivals; TechCrunch articles name none, so the list is empty. TechCabal 2018 profile returned 403. Series B lead is AXA IM Alts per TechCrunch; some outlets say co-led. The 2017 seed of 2M USD with Y Combinator and Tencent is added from Techpoint Africa, a single outlet (Seedtable has the same 2M in Aug 2017 and DigestAfrica says Oct 15, 2017, so the month is unresolved and the date is recorded as 2017).
